scenes.tts: The first film followed blue D N A into green messenger R N A and a red amino acid chain. If a D N A letter changes, how much of that chain changes? Keep watching the same blocks and reading window.
scenes.caption: The first film followed blue DNA into green messenger RNA and a red amino acid chain. If a DNA letter changes, how much of that chain changes? Keep watching the same blocks and reading window.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's colour map exactly: DNA blue; mRNA green; ribosome gold; tRNA purple; amino acids red. Rebuild its carried blue-to-green-to-red path. A blue letter block begins to wobble while the gold reading window tracks along the green strip.
scenes.narration: The first film followed blue DNA into green messenger RNA and a red amino acid chain. If a DNA letter changes, how much of that chain changes? Keep watching the same blocks and reading window.

scenes.visual: Keep the wobbling blue block behind the brief title 'When the Reading Changes'. Clear the title and enlarge the block row.

scenes.tts: A mutation is a change in D N A base order. A substitution swaps a base. Because several codons can mean the same amino acid, a swap can leave the chain unchanged. Another swap can change an amino acid or create an early stop.
scenes.caption: A mutation is a change in DNA base order. A substitution swaps a base. Because several codons can mean the same amino acid, a swap can leave the chain unchanged. Another swap can change an amino acid or create an early stop.
scenes.visual: Show a blue substitution moving into the same position. Transform the paired green codon beneath it. Run three schematic outcomes through the gold window in place: SAME amino acid, CHANGED amino acid, then STOP. Reset fully between outcomes.
scenes.narration: A mutation is a change in DNA base order. A substitution swaps a base. Because several codons can mean the same amino acid, a swap can leave the chain unchanged. Another swap can change an amino acid or create an early stop.

scenes.tts: An insertion adds bases, and a deletion removes them. The ribosome does not see spaces between codons. It starts at its reading point and groups the message from there. Adding or removing one base inside the coding part shifts that grouping. This is called a frameshift.
scenes.caption: An insertion adds bases, and a deletion removes them. The ribosome does not see spaces between codons. It starts at its reading point and groups the message from there. Adding or removing one base inside the coding part shifts that grouping. This is called a frameshift.
scenes.visual: Return to one continuous green strip under the gold reading window. Add one unlabelled green block above the strip and show a gap opening for it. Then remove it and show a different block poised to leave. Codon dividers breathe gently.
scenes.narration: An insertion adds bases, and a deletion removes them. The ribosome does not see spaces between codons. It starts at its reading point and groups the message from there. Adding or removing one base inside the coding part shifts that grouping. This is called a frameshift.

scenes.tts: Predict what happens when the waiting block enters near the start. Will only its codon change, or will later codons change too? Follow the dividers, not the colours.
scenes.caption: Predict what happens when the waiting block enters near the start. Will only its codon change, or will later codons change too? Follow the dividers, not the colours.
scenes.visual: Insert the waiting block but freeze all codon dividers for the question. Put the two choices above the strip: 'ONE CODON' and 'LATER CODONS TOO'. A gold pointer slowly sweeps across later groups.
scenes.narration: Predict what happens when the waiting block enters near the start. Will only its codon change, or will later codons change too? Follow the dividers, not the colours.

scenes.visual: Hold both choices. Let the gold pointer continue its slow sweep across the unchanged dividers during the thinking pause.

scenes.tts: The inserted block shifts every divider after it. The gold ribosome now reads new codons from that point. Many later amino acids can change, and an early stop may appear. Removing a base can shift the frame in the same way.
scenes.caption: The inserted block shifts every divider after it. The gold ribosome now reads new codons from that point. Many later amino acids can change, and an early stop may appear. Removing a base can shift the frame in the same way.
scenes.visual: Slide every codon divider after the insertion to a new position. Advance the strip through the gold reading window. Re-read each later codon as it passes: change its red amino-acid circle only when the new codon means a different amino acid, and let an occasional circle stay the same. The chain ends at the first stop in the new grouping. End with the first film's STOP sign (not red) forming on a downstream codon in the green strip.
scenes.narration: The inserted block shifts every divider after it. The gold ribosome now reads new codons from that point. Many later amino acids can change, and an early stop may appear. Removing a base can shift the frame in the same way.

scenes.tts: Now compare a quieter substitution. Messenger codon G A G means glutamic acid. Change its last letter, making G A A, and it still means glutamic acid. The D N A changed, but this amino acid chain did not. This outcome is called a silent mutation.
scenes.caption: Now compare a quieter substitution. Messenger codon GAG means glutamic acid. Change its last letter, making GAA, and it still means glutamic acid. The DNA changed, but this amino acid chain did not. This outcome is called a silent mutation.
scenes.visual: Reset to one green GAG codon and a red Glu circle. Swap the last green G to A, creating GAA. Run it through the gold window and keep the same Glu circle. Stamp SAME CHAIN beside the before-and-after rows.
scenes.narration: Now compare a quieter substitution. Messenger codon GAG means glutamic acid. Change its last letter, making GAA, and it still means glutamic acid. The DNA changed, but this amino acid chain did not. This outcome is called a silent mutation.

scenes.tts: Now follow the sickle substitution. The usual coding D N A reads G A G. The sickle allele reads G T G. Messenger R N A therefore reads G U G instead of G A G. The ribosome places valine instead of glutamic acid.
scenes.caption: Now follow the sickle substitution. The usual coding DNA reads GAG. The sickle allele reads GTG. Messenger RNA therefore reads GUG instead of GAG. The ribosome places valine instead of glutamic acid.
scenes.visual: Stack three carried rows: blue coding DNA changes GAG to GTG; the green mRNA below changes GAG to GUG; the red chain below swaps a Glu circle for Val. Animate one vertical highlight through the changed middle letter and amino acid.
scenes.narration: Now follow the sickle substitution. The usual coding DNA reads GAG. The sickle allele reads GTG. Messenger RNA therefore reads GUG instead of GAG. The ribosome places valine instead of glutamic acid.

scenes.tts: That changed spot can alter hemoglobin's behaviour. When oxygen is low, sickle hemoglobin can join into stiff rods. The rods can bend a soft red blood cell. A letter change has reached a whole cell.
scenes.caption: That changed spot can alter hemoglobin's behaviour. When oxygen is low, sickle hemoglobin can join into stiff rods. The rods can bend a soft red blood cell. A letter change has reached a whole cell.
scenes.visual: Transform the changed red chain into large labelled hemoglobin blobs, not molecular structures. Under an on-screen LOW OXYGEN label, the blobs join into rods marked 'schematic'. Place them inside a large round red cell and slowly bend the cell into a sickle.
scenes.narration: That changed spot can alter hemoglobin's behaviour. When oxygen is low, sickle hemoglobin can join into stiff rods. The rods can bend a soft red blood cell. A letter change has reached a whole cell.

scenes.tts: A changed letter does not guarantee a changed trait. Some substitutions keep the same amino acid. Protein effects also depend on which copies a person has and the environment. Here is the reading rule to keep. In coding D N A, swaps change one codon; frameshifts change later codons.
scenes.caption: A changed letter does not guarantee a changed trait. Some substitutions keep the same amino acid. Protein effects also depend on which copies a person has and the environment. Here is the reading rule to keep. In coding DNA, swaps change one codon; frameshifts change later codons.

Move a highlight down the path, then let the cards settle without ranking them as good or bad. On the last two sentences, show one swapped block changing one codon, then one inserted block sliding every later divider. Mark the strip 'coding part' between START and STOP.
